properties.statement:
⭐⭐ REFLOW2 SERVES ANY AGENT, BUT MOST OF ITS MECHANISMS FOR MAKING AN AGENT *USE* IT REACH ONLY ONE PRODUCT. Surfaced when Anthony corrected the scope of a brainstorm: *"it is for every reflow2 project and any agent (Claude, grok, openai, etc)."*

COUNTED ON REFLOW2'S OWN INSTALLATION, 2026-08-26:

    REACHES ANY MCP CLIENT       ~150 MCP tools, 21 served skills (`get_skill`/`list_skills`),
                                 every gap and detector, the served instructions
    REACHES CLAUDE CODE ONLY     3 hook events / 4 registrations in `.claude/settings.json`,
                                 23 slash commands in `~/.claude/commands/`,
                                 the handoff memory directory (RETIRED 2026-08-26)

📌 **A DISTINCTION THE TABLE INVITES A READER TO MISS, AND IT CHANGES WHAT IS WORTH FIXING: THE SKILLS ARE NOT IN THE RIGHT-HAND COLUMN.** All 21 are served from the binary and reachable by any MCP client — `dec:skills-served` exists precisely so they never drift from the running version. **What is Claude-Code-only is the SHORTCUT, not the skill.** A slash command is a markdown file in one product's config directory; the skill behind it answers `get_skill` for everybody.

⚠️ **BUT THE INSTINCT BEHIND THE MISREADING IS SOUND, AND THIS IS THE PART TO WORK.** A skill that is only ever REACHED through a shortcut is, in practice, available only where the shortcut exists. `fact:the-commands-cover-nine-of-twenty-skills-and-the-checkout-cannot-feel-it` already measured the shortfall from the other side. So the open question is not *"are skills portable"* — they are — but **"is a skill without a shortcut actually invoked by anyone?"**, which is `dec:idea-where-does-tool-use-actually-fail-four-layers` layer ② (recognising the moment) wearing different clothes.

🛑 THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THAT FOUR-LAYER DIAGNOSIS, AND IT WAS NOT STATED THERE: **layer ② is the layer whose only shipped mechanisms are product-specific.** `cap:skill-triggers` and the loop nudge are hooks. A grok, Cursor or Copilot session on the same design gets the tools, the skills and the detectors, and gets NONE of the triggering. **Every measurement of trigger effectiveness so far therefore describes the best-supported product and says nothing about the others.**

⭐ THE DESIGN GRAPH AND THE MCP SURFACE ARE THE ONLY THINGS EVERY PRODUCT SHARES — which is `rule:mcp-and-the-graph-are-the-only-common-ground`, settled the same day. `dec:skills-served` already made this argument for skills; a working set, a task list, a practice rule and a TRIGGER are the same shape of problem and have not had it applied.

📌 AGREED NEXT SESSION (Anthony, 2026-08-26): *"I don't like having skills that only work with claude code."* Return to this table. **The work is the right-hand column, and the first question is whether the 23 commands can be replaced by something the MCP surface can carry** — not whether the skills are portable, which they already are.

📌 STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: whether other products HAVE a hook equivalent reflow2 has simply not wired, or whether MCP is genuinely the only channel to them. Nobody has looked, and the answer decides whether this is an install-time gap or an argument for putting triggering INSIDE tool results — which `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` already argues on other grounds.
